title: Nihang Gurbakhsh Singh as Warrior and Disciple

blocks.text: This page sketches Nihang Gurbakhsh Singh as a saint-soldier whose devotion and courage were already famous in the Panth. Wherever there is a war being waged, he is described as the Singh who moves first beneath the Khalsa standard and answers the beat of the war drum without hesitation.

The narrative then grounds him in lineage and place. From his revered hands had he received Khandey-ki-Pahul from Bhai Mani Singh, he came from one village named Leel near Khemkaran, and within the Akal Takht premises did he keep his seat while facing the Guru's court in disciplined service.

By ending with these details, the page prepares the reader for the coming ordeal. Gurbakhsh Singh is not introduced as a reckless fighter, but as a deeply formed Sikh whose spiritual discipline, battlefield readiness, and public honor explain why he will soon stand at the center of the Panth's response to Abdali's violence.
